analyst_view.overall: Early view: the Tyne-Wear derby between two struggling sides. Newcastle under Matthias Jaissle were booed at home against Everton and have only 13 goals in 10 games, while Sunderland are 19th but beat Chelsea 1-0 and also have Europa League football in late November. Expect tension and fouls more than open football.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean lower: Sunderland have scored just eight goals all season and Newcastle's attack has been flat, and derbies between nervous sides are often tight. A 1-0 or 1-1 fits the form.

corners.text: The site has 9.5 corners. I agree: Newcastle will have more of the ball and work it wide, while Sunderland defend deep and break, as they did against Chelsea. Nothing points far either way.

cards.text: The numbers say 7.1 cards, which is very high even for a derby. I lean lower: it will be a heated game with Newcastle defending man-to-man and Sunderland pressing hard, so five or six bookings is likely, but seven-plus needs a lot to go wrong.

shots.text: The site has 29.0 shots. I lean lower: Newcastle created very little against Everton (first shot on target after 85 minutes), and Sunderland are a low-volume side. Derby tension usually means more fouls and fewer shots.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target. I lean lower because both attacks are among the weakest in the league in goals scored, and Sunderland may also feel the Europa League schedule. Seven on target looks right.
